what_happened: In job v3rf (a code job), the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The job is about checking new refusal rules against past requests. The user rejected a design that detects refusal-rule changes with a flag. They replaced it with this design. Add an athena subcommand that applies the reading acceptance rules to a stored request and reading and prints accept or refuse with the reason. After the checks pass, run it from both the base build and the candidate build over the last 50 real requests that have accepted readings in records. The replay result is the list of requests the candidate refuses that the base accepted. Every candidate gets the replay. When nothing changed the list is empty and costs no model call. Tests use fixture records, and one test builds a candidate-like rule change and shows the newly refused requests are listed.
cause: The reading stage turns a request for a replay check into the cheapest trigger it can think of, a flag marking rule changes. A flag depends on the producer or author to set it, so it misses the very changes it should catch. Nothing tells the reading stage that a safety check on Athena's own rules must run on every candidate against recorded data. It also does not know that comparing the base and candidate builds is cheap, needs no model call, and gives an empty list when nothing changed. A flag also has no way to prove itself in a test. Only the user knew the intended design.
prevention: Add a default to the reading stage's brief: when a request asks for a check that guards against regressions in Athena's own rules, the reading must specify an automatic check that runs on every candidate and compares base and candidate behavior over recorded real inputs. It must not rely on a flag or declaration to decide when to run. The reading should expose the behavior as a command that can be run on both builds. It should state the empty-result case and require a test showing a changed rule yields a non-empty list. Add a review question for the critic: "Could this check be skipped by someone forgetting to set a marker?"
proposed_request: Add a replay check for reading-acceptance rule changes. (1) Add an athena subcommand that applies the reading acceptance rules to a stored request and its accepted reading, and prints accept or refuse with the reason. (2) After a candidate's checks pass, run that subcommand from both the base build and the candidate build over the last 50 real requests that have accepted readings in records. The replay result is the list of requests the candidate refuses that the base accepted. (3) Run the replay for every candidate, with no flag deciding whether it runs. When no rule changed, the list is empty and the replay makes no model call. Record the result with the job. Acceptance: the verifier can run the subcommand itself on a fixture request and see accept or refuse with a reason. A test using fixture records shows an empty list when base and candidate are the same. A test builds a candidate-like rule change and shows the newly refused requests are listed. A Grep shows no flag or marker gates the replay. Do not cite the producer's report as evidence for any criterion.
